title: Americas · breeds of the new world
blurb: Canada, the United States and the working farms of the continent: sled dogs, water dogs and the farm ratters bred after the frontier closed.

items.d: Developed in the American West despite the name: a medium herder with a merle coat and endless drive.
The heavy freighting dog of Alaska's Inuit: 34–43 kg, slower than a husky and far stronger.
Canadian water dog with webbed feet and an oily coat, bred to haul nets and rescue swimmers.
American bull-and-terrier cross from Boston: 5–11 kg, tuxedo-marked and snub-nosed.
American water retriever from two shipwrecked pups in 1814: oily coat, broad chest, hard worker.
German spitz descendant from the American circus, in toy, miniature and standard sizes.
American farm ratter of the 1900s: small, quick and bred to clear a barn.
Louisiana's spotted herder and hog dog, the state dog, with webbed feet and pale eyes.
